Carte Blanche Christmas Special

By: Sinethemba Nogude | Production

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
A Carte Blanche Christmas Special

Unique Selling Point:
This year we will be a Christmas special with a difference;we will be collaborating with the Mzansi Youth Choir, as well as telling the incredible story of amateur opera singer Mthetho Mapoyi.

Summary:
Ngwelezana Tertiary hospital close to Empangeni is the only hospital in the Umhlathuze Municipality to offer specialist treatment to people in the region, currently all 18 district hospitals refer their burns patients (many of them needing paediatric care) to Ngwelezana – this In spite of the scarcity of paediatric beds available. The hospital has become a referral centre for children who have suffered burns, trauma requiring surgery and orthopaedic care.
Being a poverty stricken part of KZN many households in areas such as Empangeni,Eshowe, Richards Bay,KwaMbonambi,Melmoth,Mthunzini Nkandla Gingindlovu still use firewood as fuel or paraffin stoves , making burns a frequent injury in Ngwelezana- T
Currently, all paediatric burns and trauma patients at Ngwelezana Hospital are treated in the Adult Burns Ward which is ill-equipped to deal with specialised paediatric care-the Burns Ward is in a terrible state, it is dilapidated with aging equipment which simply cannot meet the needs of the patients- truly there is a desperate need for a dedicated Paediatric unit at the hospital.- The desperate need for this new facility will also be reflected
Now the Carte Blanche ‘MAD’ campaign is taking on this challenge ( which will be the 19th hospital project ) , and work is underway in creating a new dedicated Paediatric Unit, this will be done by renovating and converting one of the hospital’s buildings.

As we head towards a milestone – Our 19th hospital project ( including our second Burns Unit- the first being Kalefong) he insert will encapsulate the spirit of the ‘Making a Difference’ campaign and why it came to existence in the first place.

Further information:
The Mzansi Youth Choir was established in July 2003 with the aim of affording talented, underprivileged teenagers and young adults (14-24 years) the opportunity to proficiently perform locally and abroad. The choir consists of 45 choristers from Soweto and other areas in and around Johannesburg.

The word Mzansi means “south” in isiZulu and is also the township slang word for South Africa. The choir’s repertoire is an exciting assortment of South African music which incorporates elements of traditional music, pop and jazz.
The Mzansi Youth Choir is widely regarded as the best show choir in the country. Performance highlights include the One World Music Festival, M-Net Idols, Huisgenoot Skouspel, Starlight Classics, The Voice, The Presidential Inauguration, KKNK, The National Arts Festival, The South African Music Awards, as well as performances with the Andrea Bocelli, Josh Groban and Celtic Women.

During the 2010 FIFA World Cup, the choir shared the stage with Columbian superstar Shakira and local band Freshly Ground for the performance of the official World Cup song ‘WakaWaka’ at the Kick-Off Concert as well as the World Cup Final.

International highlights include performances in Canada (Stratford Summer Music Festival), Denmark (AAVF, Europe’s largest contemporary vocal festival), England (Celtic Festival, Guildhall), Turkey, Scotland (Commonwealth Games, Mandela Day Celebrations) and Russia (Cultural exchange – Russian and South African governments).

In April 2017, the choir performed at the International Youth Choir Festival at the Royal Albert Hall, London. The Mzansi Youth Choir was the only choir from the African continent to be selected to perform at this prestigious global event.

Mzansi’s beautiful and youthful sound, exciting choreography, pulsating energy, buoyancy, vibrancy and devotion to South African music is an experience not to be missed.


Mapoyi Mthetho an opera singer stunned customers at a local restaurant 'Ons Huisie' in Bloubergstrand.

Mthetho sang the famous Nessun Dorma and guests were left gasping for more.a Pavarotti album which he listened to repeatedly while growing up. Having only this music soundtracking his youth in the rural Xhosa township in South Africa’s Western Cape, Mthetho taught himself to sing along – not only in Italian, but with similar richness and timber to the original. Mthetho, whose first language is isiXhosa, never knew the direct translations of what he was singing, but felt the meaning through the music.

Script:


/O South Africa has produced an enviable list of international Opera talents such as Sibongile Khumalo, Pretty Yende and Phumeza Matshikiza. Now amateur singer Mthetho Maphoyi is hoping to join their ranks as our next rising star.
V/O Living from hand to mouth as a street performer in Cape Town Mthetho regularly impressed onlookers with his breath-taking voice.
V/O In a video the 30 year old from Kwelihle township in Hermanus serenaded a crowd at a Cape Town restaurant and it went viral, winning the hearts of South Africans . The video was viewed over 480 000 times and shared over 10 000 times on Facebook.
V/O Mthetho attributes his passion for music to the two most important women in his life-his late mother Lumka and grandmother Nomaslams Maphoyi and despite Mthetho’s father walking out on him and his mother when he was just four years old, he is grateful for the gift of music he left behind.
My love for music came from my mother, my mother loved music My mother had cds my father used to listen to/ I would say the CDs are the only things he left behind,because I wouldn’t say he did much for me -she had a lot of cds she would listen - When my mother would play the cds I would sing along even though I didn’t even know the meaning of the lyrics. Santa Lucia was the first one I could sing along to I was nine at the time. . At Home my grandmother would make us sing before we prayed; I would lead them because I had a good voice.
V/O A prodigy at the age of 12 he formed an opera group called the ‘ 6 Tenors’ with his friends,paying homage to his idol Luciano Pavarotti They performed at tourist hotspots all around Hermanus.
when I see Pavarotti performing he had a huge audience-people Peoplewere appreciative and I wanted to be like him
(C0015)// every year there is a Whale festival each year in September, people are very creative they would come with crafts and sell them, but we could only sing, we would get money and we would contribute at home -that motivated me. The way people appreciate the music .
V
V/O His passion and determination eventually paid off .In 2008 he was invited to study at the prestigious Guild Hall School of Music and Drama in London.
V/O But the excitement was short lived, a month before he was due to leave for England Mthetho was badly injured whilst trying to stop a fight.He was slashed from cheek to neck
I got this injury at the wrong time ,I got it on the 31st of July in 2008 . I was due to leave to study at the Guild Hall School of Music in London ,but I got stabbed by my cousin.I got to hospital I was only helped the following day, I could have died of blood loss.
V/O Just as he was recovering Mthetho received the most telling blow- his mother passed on.
My mother was everything to me, From that day on I was never the same; I took drugs, I was never home, I wouldn’t listen to anyone. I would cry all the time; I didn’t see the point of living. I even thought about taking my own life.
V/O His dream lay in tatters but Mthetho gained strength from the memory of his mother and his passion for music, performing to anyone who was willing to listen.
V/OHis moment came when this video him was spotted by businessman Bruce Wienand who was touched by Mthetho’s rendition of Nessun Dorma .He arranged an all-expenses paid trip to Dubai where he got the opportunity to feed his dream .
V/O With every performance he is determined to make his mother and grandmother proud.
I think of them when I sing, I think of them before I go on stage, I ask for their blessings because I know they are looking down on me from where they are. Even when I speak to them and don’t get a response I can still feel their spirit.
V/O Currently unemployed, Mthetho Still dreams of becoming a world renowned opera singer, performing at prestigious opera houses. Carte Blanche Invited Mthetho to the magnificent Soweto theatre for a performance –This is his gift to South Africa.
//02:53 when I sing I forget I’m singing for money, I feel happy .Sometimes I feel Like I’m in that century wearing those costume,I’m in the 17th or 18th century. All I can say is that when sing I am not singing for myself, I am singing for you.
